clue.text: Pater's home, regrettably in mood!

indicators.note: something done regrettably has gone wrong, so the letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A sad scene: Father's house is in a gloomy mood, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Pater is old public-school slang for father; it is only fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the prevailing feeling or tone of a place, a close synonym of mood.

clue.text: According to Italian, one pack animal's lost its dam

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: lost means no longer had, so the mother is taken out

parts.note: a llama is a South American pack animal
a dam is an animal's mother, and ma is mother

explanation.surface: An Italian account of a pack animal that has lost its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Dam looks like a river barrier; here it is a mother animal, MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alla is the Italian phrase meaning in the manner of or according to, as in alla marcia.

clue.text: Surrender post and disturb ace team

parts.note: to move something is to disturb it from its place
A is the card abbreviation for ace
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Someone resigns their job and upsets a top team.
explanation.definitionFit: To move aside is to step down and let someone else take your position, giving up a job.

clue.text: Songs — only for basses, you might say?

indicators.note: said out loud, so the phrase is replaced by words that sound like the answer

parts.note: songs only for basses are very deep ones, which might be called 'so lows'

explanation.surface: Musical pieces suitable only for the bass voices of a choir.
explanation.walkthrough: Said as two words, so-lows describes music pitched for the deepest singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Solos are songs or pieces performed by a single singer.

clue.text: Dressed a snack in topping of harissa and died

indicators.note: in places the snack inside the other letters
the topping is what lies on top, so the first letter of harissa

parts.note: supplies its first letter
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A snack served with a harissa topping, after which the diner died.
explanation.walkthrough: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Habited is an old word for clothed, especially in a monk's or nun's habit.

clue.text: Schedule some urgent orthopaedics for muscle

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties
some marks a part: these letters run from the end of urgent into the start of orthopaedics

explanation.surface: A hospital booking of urgent bone and joint treatment for a damaged muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that turns a limb, as in the rotator cuff of the shoulder.

clue.text: Start to appear in Twitter?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is to begin to show, as the sun ... over the horizon
second meaning: the small cry of a bird, a twitterer

explanation.walkthrough: Twitter looks like the social network; here it means a bird that twitters, and its cry is the answer. Like every theme answer it reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the first faint showing of something and the tiny chirp a young bird makes.

clue.text: No exclamation of surprise when Heather enjoys Lark in the Clear Air

indicators.note: enjoying a lark is having fun, so the remaining letters frolic into a new order
no means without, so the exclamation is taken away

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter
ah is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: A singer called Heather loves performing the song The Lark in the Clear Air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lark in the Clear Air is a traditional Irish song. Taking A and H from HEATHER leaves HETER, which 'enjoys Lark' then rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The ether is a poetic term for the clear upper sky or heavens.

clue.text: Above airfield, ace from British Flying Circus identifies 6 and 10 companions

indicators.note: in a down clue the first part sits above the second

parts.note: Michael Palin was a star of the British comedy series Monty Python's Flying Circus
a drome is an informal word for an airfield or aerodrome

explanation.surface: A wartime-sounding picture of a top pilot of a flying circus over an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Flying Circus suggests aerobatic pilots, but it is the TV comedy show. This answer names the theme: 6 (PEEP) and 10 (LEVEL) read the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: PEEP and LEVEL are both words spelt the same backwards and forwards, so they are fellow examples of this kind of word.

clue.text: Peripheral support from Mike over river protection

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Ouse is an English river
a pad is protective padding

explanation.surface: Backing from someone called Mike, who is above river protection works.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouse is a computer peripheral, and a mousepad is the mat that supports it.

clue.text: Plane gaining some remarkable velocity

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An aircraft picking up a remarkable speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane in geometry is a flat surface, and level means flat, so a level is a plane; gaining is part of that phrase in this reading.

clue.text: Promise of match, live, run by Henry

indicators.note: by means alongside, so Henry's name sits next to the run

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
to trot is to run at a gentle pace
Hal is the familiar short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A sports promise: the match will be shown live, with Henry in charge of the running.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is an engagement, a promise of a future marriage, and a match is a marriage.

clue.text: Flier damages nose of helicopter — idiot ignoring warnings at departure

parts.note: to mar is to damage, so damages gives mars

indicators.note: the nose is the front, so the first letter of helicopter

parts.note: supplies its first letter

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so one letter is dropped from the idiot

parts.note: a twit is a fool or idiot

indicators.note: a departure is where a journey starts, so the first letter of warnings

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Something flying damages a helicopter's nose; the fool ignored the warnings before take-off.
explanation.walkthrough: Flier is the definition, a bird, not the helicopter. TWIT loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: The marsh tit is a small European bird, and a flier is anything that flies.

clue.text: Father provided name for Lorelei, say?

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of a horse

explanation.surface: Did Dad supply the name Lorelei for his daughter?
explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei is the Rhine maiden of German legend whose singing lured boatmen onto the rocks; 'say' marks her as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive female creature who lures sailors with song, and the Lorelei is a classic example.

clue.text: Risks coming, partially from future shock

parts.note: an advent is an arrival or coming
partially marks a part: these letters run from the end of future into the start of shock

explanation.surface: Dangers are on the way, partly arising from a shock to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Adventures can mean hazardous undertakings or ventures, which are risks.

clue.text: One almost ready to appear in performance is idolised

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be found inside it, so these letters go inside the performance

parts.note: a deed is an act or performance
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: fit means ready or prepared

explanation.surface: Someone nearly ready to go on stage is worshipped by the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' minus its last letter is the trap: ready is FIT, and 'almost' trims it; 'performance' is a deed, not a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify is to make a god of someone, so deified means worshipped or idolised.

clue.text: Among facts exposed, setter's still…

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: a word exposed has its outer layer stripped, so its first and last letters go

parts.note: loses its outer letters
the setter is I, and setter's means I have, I've

explanation.surface: With the facts laid bare, the setter remains calm, the sentence carrying on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 18-down; still is an adjective, motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means not moving or doing anything, the same as being motionless.

clue.text: Freshen up decor in Harvester, including paintwork at entrance

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so a letter goes into the harvester

parts.note: a reaper harvests crops

indicators.note: the entrance is where you begin, so the first letter of paintwork

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Smartening up the décor at a Harvester restaurant, with paint at the entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvester looks like the British pub-restaurant chain; here it is a reaper.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaper a room is to hang new wallpaper, a way of refreshing its decoration.

clue.text: …set, from leak about old politician, to receive promotion

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the leak goes round what follows
to receive is to take in, so these letters are held inside

parts.note: pour means flow out, as a leak does
an MP is a Member of Parliament
an ad is an advertisement, a promotion

explanation.surface: Carrying on from 16-down, the setter is ready to be promoted from a leak about a past politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Set is a hairdressing noun here; Madame de Pompadour gave her name to the swept-up hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a hairstyle swept up high from the forehead, and a set is a styled arrangement of hair.

clue.text: They say the setter used to be hard — that's bunkum!

indicators.note: what they say is heard spoken, so the setter's word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
was is the past of be
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter boasts of having once been tough, and is told that is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is a slang word for nonsense or humbug, the same idea as bunkum.

clue.text: In Gunners' case, they — lacking wingers — lost badly, right?

indicators.note: something done badly is muddled, so the letters are rearranged
wingers are the outside players, so the outer letters of they go

parts.note: loses its first and last letters
fodder taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the Gunners, lost badly without their wide players, didn't they?
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is the nickname of Arsenal football club; here gunners are people with guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A holster is the leather case in which a gun is carried.

clue.text: A greeting for Eve from two ladies touring India?

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the two ladies go round the letter for India

parts.note: a lady is a madam, so two ladies give madam twice
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Two women on a trip to India greet someone called Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the famous palindrome supposedly spoken by Adam on meeting Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Madam, I'm Adam' is the traditional first introduction of Adam to Eve in the Garden of Eden.

clue.text: Airmen disconcerted, taking apex of temple for tower

indicators.note: taking means adding on, so the next letter joins the rearranged airmen
disconcerted means thrown into confusion, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter

indicators.note: the apex is the top, so the first letter of temple

parts.note: supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Flustered pilots clip the top of a temple and hit a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A minaret is the slender tower of a mosque from which the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: Opinion among statesmen varied, following fractious mass walk-out

indicators.note: varied means changed about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
fractious means unruly, so the letters of mass leave in any order
a walk-out is a departure, so these letters are removed from the statesmen

parts.note: the fodder letter for letter
the letters taken out

explanation.surface: A political view among varied statesmen, after an angry mass walk-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M, A, S, S from STATESMEN to leave TTEEN, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, close to an opinion.

clue.text: Nick's grown up, then?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a nick is a small cut, and the 's is just 'is'
second meaning, read cryptically: split as ..., not a child (CH abbreviates child), so grown up

explanation.surface: Is young Nick an adult now?
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NOT CH, the answer says not a child, which is grown up.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small V-shaped cut, the same as a nick.

clue.text: Must this official decide who's in pole position?

definitions.text: Must this official decide who's in pole position?

parts.words: Must this official decide who's in pole position?
parts.note: pole position sounds like motor racing, but the official meant works up telephone poles, and a sports line official judges positions too

explanation.walkthrough: Pole position is the front of a racing grid; here it is someone up a telegraph pole, the worker who repairs overhead lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A linesman is both a sports official on the touchline and a worker who maintains telephone or power lines.

clue.text: Information from ship transporting junk

indicators.note: a ship transporting cargo holds it inside

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
tat is cheap junk

explanation.surface: Details from a vessel carrying a cargo of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Junk looks like a Chinese sailing ship beside 'ship'; it is rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stats is short for statistics, numerical data or information.

clue.text: See 21
Tiller Girl is next to weaken, given unending violent disturbance

indicators.note: next to means alongside, so the girl's name follows the weakening

parts.note: to rot is to decay and weaken
Ava is a girl's name

indicators.note: without its ends means both outer letters go

parts.note: a storm is a violent disturbance

explanation.surface: A dancer in the Tiller Girls troupe is about to fade, after some violent upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tiller Girls were a famous British precision dance troupe; here a tiller is a machine that tills soil. STORM loses its ends to give TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotavator is a motorised machine with rotating blades for breaking up soil, a kind of tiller.

clue.text: Bypass daughter is given after alveoli regularly fail

indicators.note: given after means placed at the end, after the other letters
letters that fail at regular intervals drop out every other time, leaving alternate letters

parts.note: supplies its first, third, fifth and seventh letters
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A medical note: a bypass operation because a daughter's lung tissue keeps failing.
explanation.walkthrough: Bypass looks like a heart operation; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to go round it rather than through it, which is to avoid it.

clue.text: Laggards in class to watch video call

indicators.note: laggards come last, so the final letter of each of the next words

parts.note: gives its last letter
gives its last letter
gives its last letter
gives its last letter

explanation.surface: The slow pupils in class get to watch a video call.
explanation.walkthrough: Video call looks like a phrase; call alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: So-ho is an old hunting cry, a call to draw attention to a hare that has been sighted.

clue.text: Trust he's off alcohol — getting treatment, to be honest

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken letter for letter
fodder is just he; the 's is read as 'has' joining it to the anagram signal
rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A worried hope that someone off the drink is getting help, honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Trust he' is rearranged: the 's of he's joins it to 'off', the anagram signal, so the S is not part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A truth serum is a drug supposed to make a person speak honestly when questioned, so a treatment to be honest.
